screening_reasoning: Retraction notice with no abstract; not a computational tool, system, or harness for literature workflow. Pure editorial artifact lacking computational architecture or empirical evaluation.

EcoXAI is a modular, containerized multi-agent system for biomedical discovery with explicit pipeline execution stages, knowledge graph integration, and hallucination mitigation. Provides GitHub codebase, quantitative evaluation (103 drug candidates, 79 novel candidates identified), and architectural transparency. Directly addresses all three RQs.

Narrative review/commentary on LLM adoption in medical publishing; proposes policy frameworks (disclosure systems, AI co-editor model) but does not implement or evaluate a computational literature review harness. No system architecture or empirical evaluation of a tool.

Systematic review and taxonomy of AI for cardiovascular diagnosis; no computational tool or harness proposed for literature discovery/screening/extraction. No abstract available but title indicates review article, not system implementation.

Published in 2010, well before the 2023 temporal boundary for LLM-era literature review harnesses. While it describes a classifier for systematic review screening, it predates LLMs and modern agentic AI entirely.

Diagnostic study evaluating LLM accuracy for data extraction in a specific clinical domain (cardiovascular exercise rehabilitation); not a literature review harness or tool for general academic evidence synthesis. No system architecture or reusable pipeline proposed.

Systematic review of LLM performance in data extraction; evaluates existing tools but does not propose or implement a new computational harness for literature workflow. No novel system architecture or codebase.

Systematic review and meta-analysis of LLM performance in automated medical literature screening; evaluates existing approaches but does not propose a new tool, harness, or multi-agent pipeline. No computational artifact contributed.

Randomized crossover trial evaluating an LLM-assisted data extraction system (OpenAI o3) for emerging infectious disease evidence reviews. Provides protocol, source code, and data on GitHub; reports quantitative metrics (completion time, accuracy). Addresses RQ2 (evidence-trust via accuracy validation) and RQ3 (empirical evaluation via RCT).

Proposes and benchmarks a fully local, schema-constrained LLM pipeline (gpt-oss-20b via Ollama) for abstract screening and evidence mapping. Provides deterministic metadata filtering, LLM-assisted screening, structured extraction, and audit-adjusted performance metrics against three published systematic reviews. Includes codebase and quantitative evaluation (precision, recall, F1).

Introduces ImpleMATE, an AI-enabled platform for implementation science (evidence extraction, contextual analysis, barrier identification). While it uses LLMs and addresses evidence synthesis, it targets implementation research practice, not academic literature discovery/screening/extraction workflows specifically. Domain is healthcare implementation, not scholarly literature review.
Study of ChatGPT response consistency on medical examination questions; general-purpose LLM evaluation in medical education, not a literature review harness or tool for academic evidence synthesis.
Published in 2021, before the 2023 temporal boundary. COVID-19 epidemiological study using random sample testing; no connection to AI-assisted literature review harnesses.

Narrative review of AI in systematic reviews and meta-analyses; summarizes task-specific performance and residual error quantification across existing tools but does not propose or implement a new computational harness. No novel system architecture or codebase.
Graph neural network-based fault localization for software engineering (DepGraph); targets code debugging, not academic literature discovery, screening, or evidence synthesis. Non-scholarly domain.

LatteReview is a Python-based multi-agent framework for systematic review automation using LLMs. Modular agents for title/abstract screening, relevance scoring, structured data extraction; supports RAG, multimodal reviews, Pydantic validation, async processing. Available on GitHub with documentation and installable package. Directly implements a literature review harness with provenance and evaluation.

Technical survey of contextual enrichment in LLMs (in-context learning, RAG, GraphRAG, CausalRAG); provides literature-screening protocol and claim-audit framework but is a survey/manifesto, not a computational tool or harness for literature review workflows. No system implementation.

Evidence-synthesis framework for evaluating/governing/orchestrating agentic AI; contributes a four-layer framework, ODTA runtime-placement test, and action-evidence bundle. While relevant to AI governance, it does not implement a literature review harness for academic evidence synthesis. Framework paper without computational tool for literature workflow.

M-Reason: multi-agent system for auditable biomedical evidence synthesis (cancer research). Specialized agents for evidence retrieval, appraisal, synthesis; emphasizes explainability, structured reporting, user auditability, traceability from source to conclusions. Interactive UI available. Implements computational harness with provenance and trust mechanisms.

HySemRAG: hybrid semantic RAG framework for automated literature synthesis and methodological gap analysis. Eight-stage pipeline: metadata acquisition, PDF retrieval, Docling-based layout analysis, bibliographic management, LLM extraction, topic modeling, semantic unification, knowledge graph construction. Agentic self-correction with QA, post-hoc citation verification (99% accuracy). Dual data products (Neo4j KG, Qdrant vectors). Quantitative evaluation on 643 observations. Comprehensive literature review harness.
